deals.headline: Da Silva pays the $70m MLS expansion fee for Orlando City
deals.summary: Brazilian entrepreneur Flávio Augusto da Silva, majority owner since 2013, paid the $70m expansion fee; the club debuted in MLS in 2015. Pre-2015; listed for context.

deals.evidence: The Wilf family has finalized its acquisition of Orlando City Soccer Club, becoming the Club’s new majority owners, it was announced today.
deals.headline: Wilf family completes purchase of Orlando City, Orlando Pride and the stadium
deals.investor: Wilf family (with the DeVos family as limited partner)
deals.summary: Majority acquisition including the MLS club, NWSL's Orlando Pride, the stadium and training facilities; the Wilfs dissolved their minority stake in Nashville SC. Sportico reported before signing that the deal would likely close in the $400m-$450m range depending on structure; no final price was published.

stadium_owner.detail: Club-owned: the stadium (then Exploria Stadium) was included in the Wilf family's 2021 acquisition of the club. Opened March 2017, 100% privately funded at a cost of $155m. Naming partner Inter&Co (Inter.co).
stadium_owner.evidence: The purchase includes Orlando City Soccer Club of Major League Soccer, the Orlando Pride of the National Women’s Soccer League, Exploria Stadium and all related soccer assets

founded_evidence: In 2010, Phil Rawlins, founder and former owner of the Austin Aztex, ceased operation in Texas and moved to Orlando to join a group called Orlando Pro Soccer.
name: Orlando City Soccer Club
notes: Stadium renamed Inter.co Stadium (formerly Exploria, then Inter&Co Stadium); the earlier record's 25,500 capacity (Wikipedia) is replaced by the stadium's own 24,453. Founded 2010 = the year the Orlando Pro Soccer club was set up per the club's own history article (USL era); MLS debut 2015. Forbes 2026 figures are 2025-season estimates via the Internet Archive snapshot (Forbes 403s); Forbes ranks the club #27, key owner Wilf family. The 2021 sale price is only a pre-signing press range ($400m-$450m, Sportico), so the deal amount is left null. No CEO/president, attendance, socials, sponsor, legal entity or honours sourced.
